board.title: How Maglev Trains Float on Thin Air

scenes.narration: A five-hundred-ton bullet train can float two inches above its guideway with zero wheels touching the track. How does it defeat gravity?
The secret lies in liquid-helium-cooled electromagnets. Chilled to negative four hundred and fifty degrees Fahrenheit, their electrical resistance vanishes completely.
scenes.label: -450 F

scenes.narration: Without resistance, massive persistent currents circulate endlessly, generating magnetic fields tens of thousands of times stronger than Earth's magnetic field.
As the train glides along, these fields induce mirror magnetic poles in the track wall. Because identical poles repel, the upward push levitates the heavy chassis.
Floating entirely on a cushion of pure magnetic flux eliminates all rolling friction, pushing the train to three hundred and seventy miles per hour.
